a.s26221: Arno "Doc" As unpacked a child's drawing of a horse at R-C5. The man in the next bunk shifted his bag to make room without asking what it was. The new duty roster listed Arno "Doc" As as a signaller. He kept checking the old roster until someone took it down.
alexgreve: Norbert Alexgreve arrived with the Day 9 draft, carrying his brother's pocket watch and the news from home, which was old by the time he told it.
jankiedestroyer: By the time Quentin "Saint" Jankiedestro reached Q-F8, the war was 9 days old and had its own habits. He learned the first one within the hour: keep your head down.
klecka2617: Teodor Klecka came up with a draft of replacements on Day 6. Nobody asked his name until the third night. After that, everyone knew it. Victory at Hill 304. Teodor Klecka let himself talk about leave for the first time in days.

Teodor Klecka hauled ammunition boxes up the communication trench all night. His back filed a formal complaint. A letter from home reached Teodor Klecka before dusk. Teodor Klecka read it twice and slept a little easier.

Shellfire stopped the carrying party at a trench junction. Teodor Klecka waited under a load that got heavier by the minute. A letter from home reached Teodor Klecka before dusk. Teodor Klecka read it twice and slept a little easier.
A borrowed towel came back cleaner than when Teodor Klecka lent it. He is considering lending out the rest of the washing.
Teodor Klecka traded a cigarette for a pinch of salt. Supper improved. The argument about the exchange rate did not.
nazareth_2bc: In Dunmarrow, Edmund "Saint" Nazareth was a ferryman. In R-C14, he is a number and a rifle. He has told everyone he intends to be a ferryman again.
noaskevitch: Nils Noaskevitch reported to S-F2 with a photograph gone soft at the edges sewn into his tunic lining. The sergeant pretended not to notice.
Nils Noaskevitch took a wrong turn at two identical trench junctions. He decided the route needed names that could be remembered under pressure.

Nils Noaskevitch and Wendel Jesus compared drawings of home. Both drawings included a kitchen table larger than the house. Victory at Hill 304. Nils Noaskevitch let himself talk about leave for the first time in days.
Nils Noaskevitch marked the first junction with a spoon and the second with a boot sole. Other runners have begun using the names in their directions.
Nils Noaskevitch can fall asleep anywhere, instantly. Today, under fire at the Hanging Bridge, that habit was the only steady thing in S-F2.
Someone removed the spoon from Nils Noaskevitch's junction to eat supper. He retrieved it and nailed it above comfortable reaching height.
A new runner delivered a message using Spoon Corner and Boot Turn without hesitation. Nils Noaskevitch drew both markers on the official route sketch.
padraiggallagher: By the time Tobias Padraiggalla reached S-C13, the war was 9 days old and had its own habits. He learned the first one within the hour: keep your head down.
zde_schu: After 4 days of war, R-F22 had a place for everything. On Day 5, the men rearranged a shelf to make a place for Silas Schu.

Silas Schu crawled out with the wiring party. When a flare went up, he lay still and counted to ten. The wire at R-F22 holds again. News of the loss of Hill 304 reached R-F22 with the rations. Silas Schu ate while listening to the revised orders.
A bullet found Silas Schu at R-F22, high in the shoulder. He went down hard and stayed down. Shot by Matthias Universal of the Hegemony (@chamra_universal).
Silas Schu spent the day on a stretcher outside the aid post, waiting for a bed to come free. The bearers brought water twice.
Silas Schu asked the bearers for water and then for his mother. He died before either came.
Marek "Owl" Schu joined R-F22 under the shadow of Silas Schu's name. At the first roll call, the corporal used the right one.
Somebody hung a doorbell on the next dugout. Marek "Owl" Schu went to look. It was a spoon tied to an empty tin.
